abstract: Activating mutations in leucine-rich repeat kinase 2 (LRRK2) are among the most common genetic risk factors for Parkinson's disease. LRRK2 phosphorylates a subset of Rab GTPases at a conserved Ser/Thr residue within the switch 2 alpha-helix, disrupting interactions with canonical regulators and effectors while promoting recruitment of phospho-specific effectors, including RILPL1, RILPL2, JIP3 and JIP4. However, the full spectrum of phosphorylation-dependent Rab interactions remains unknown. Here, we used mass spectrometry to characterise the phospho-Rab interactome. Purified pRab1, pRab3, pRab8, pRab12, pRab35 and pRab43, together with pRab7, a substrate of the related kinase LRRK1, were used as baits in cellular pulldowns. Comparison with non-phosphorylated Rab interactomes identified numerous phosphorylation-dependent binding proteins, alongside known and candidate effectors that preferentially bound non-phosphorylated Rabs, consistent with phosphorylation broadly disrupting Rab complexes. A prominent phospho-selective interactor was TBC1D2 which bound to multiple phosphorylated Rabs. TBC1D2 is a Rab7 GTPase-activating protein (GAP) implicated in LRRK1-dependent regulation of endolysosomal dynamics. AlphaFold modeling, mutagenesis, co-immunoprecipitation and biophysical analyses demonstrated that a conserved di-lysine motif within a central coiled-coil domain of TBC1D2 mediates binding to pRab3A and pRab8A. These findings identify TBC1D2 as a phospho-Rab effector and suggest a molecular link between LRRK2-dependent Rab phosphorylation and Rab GAP function. Our phospho-Rab interaction resource provides a foundation for investigating how LRRK2 regulates membrane trafficking.
